incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 8, 16, 49, 101, 106, 114, and 127
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada); Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) for extra-provincial registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001 under the CBCA) and Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors (Form 4002)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required under the CBCA; incorporator may establish authorized share capital with nominal consideration; escrow account not required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby confirms the subscription for common shares by the founding shareholder and authorizes the issuance of such shares in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be established at the address set forth in the Articles, and the designated records office shall be located in Alberta. RESOLVED, that the individuals named in Form 4002 are appointed as the first directors, and the following officers are elected: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED, that management is authorized to execute all filings, open bank accounts, and take all necessary steps for the Corporation's incorporation and operational commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation (NUANS Name Search Report)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via the NUANS online portal (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through the NUANS system for a proposed corporate name (e.g., 'Hardcore MMORPG Global Inc.') to obtain a Name Search Report; review for conflicts and, if desired, reserve the name for up to 90 days. Payment is made online via credit card or interac; the name report is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and up to three alternative names
Credit card or approved payment method for filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicting, file a revised name request with a new NUANS report; or seek a consent from the conflicting name holder; or proceed under a numbered company name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (online filing via Corporations Canada's e-filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) via the Corporations Canada online e-filing system; require the name, registered office address, share structure, directors, and any restrictions. Pay the $200 filing fee online; the system will issue a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval. Additionally, for the purpose of extra-provincial registration in Alberta, file with the Alberta Corporate Registry for an extra-provincial licence.
required_dossiers: Notification of Registered Office and First Directors (Form 4002)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada rejects the Articles (e.g., missing clauses or unpaid fees), resubmit the corrected Articles within the prescribed time; any rejected filing is returned with instructions for correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Federal Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of Form 4001, Corporations Canada issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The Certificate is conclusive evidence of corporate existence. The corporation must then file Form 4002 for the initial registered office and first board of directors, and ensure the registered office is physically located in Alberta or another CBCA jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation received from Corporations Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is not issued due to incomplete or inconsistent data, file updated correction documents with Corporations Canada and pay any correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting of the initial directors to adopt the first board resolution approving share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments; pass a by-law (optional) and adopt corporate records. Ensure the resolution is minuted and signed in accordance with the CBCA and corporate records regulations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is challenged, execute unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting and ensure all directors and shareholders approve or ratify the resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since the corporation is incorporated federally (CBCA) and intends to carry on business in Alberta, register as an extra-provincial corporation with the Alberta Corporate Registry by filing the required application and paying the prescribed fee. Obtain the extra-provincial certificate or Alberta corporate accessory number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Status from Corporations Canada
Alberta address for service (registered office address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extra-provincial registration is delayed or queried, correct the registration form and resubmit; if the registered address is non-compliant, change it and file notice with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining business number (CRA) and corporate tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO); the BN enables GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax accounts. The corporation must also obtain an Alberta Corporate Tax Account if applicable. Register using the Certificate of Incorporation and the corporation's registered office address.
required_dossiers: CRA registration form or BRO account request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests clarification, respond via BRO or written notice within 30 days; ensure all beneficial ownership and director identities are provided.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial bank account and share capital subscription execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or financial institution; corporate secretary and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, the initial resolution, the registered office address, and director identification. Fund the bank account with the subscribed share capital and issue share certificates accordingly. Maintain capital ledger entries.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank query arises regarding beneficial ownership, provide an updated corporate registry and beneficial ownership register; ensure KYC documents are in order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Agency (AGLC) for any virtual currency or gambling-like mechanics if applicable; otherwise no industrial licensing board for software publishing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general software or MMORPG operating license required in Alberta for pure software publishing; if the game includes loot boxes or gambling-like mechanics, consider AGLC permits

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA); federal Environmental Protection Agency (Environment and Climate Change Canada) if applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for software publishing (ISIC 5820) as no physical manufacturing facility; environmental registration not required without physical operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital MMORPG publishing; if physical offices are established, comply with municipal waste and building codes and Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act for any physical operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to digital software publishing; if physical premises are occupied, obtain fire safety certification from local fire department, structural load inspection from municipal building authority, and workplace safety clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada); primary online gateways: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA) via Canada.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta business corporation first completes incorporation or extra-provincial registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry, then obtains a federal Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST program account (RT suffix) from CRA by filing Form RC1 (or online through BRO with an appointed Canadian representative and Form RC59). Non-resident suppliers of remote digital services (digital game downloads, subscriptions, in-app purchases) can use CRA's simplified electronic registration for non-resident digital service suppliers; CRA issues a 9-digit BN plus RT program account as the sole tax identifier. Canada does not operate a separate VAT ID system; the GST/HST account number is the mandatory identifier on invoices and returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (non-pass-through). A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxable person under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no check-the-box or pass-through classification election is available. Corporate income is taxed at entity level, and Canadian-resident shareholders receive integration only via the eligible dividend tax credit; the corporation is also a GST/HST registrant in its own right.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not recognise IRC 7701-style entity classification elections. Statutory elections available to a CA_CORP include: (i) Income Tax Act s. 85 transfer election for tax-deferred rollover of assets into the corporation; (ii) s. 89 eligible dividend designation to manage the dividend tax credit; (iii) Excise Tax Act s. 240 optional GST/HST registration for small suppliers and s. 148 Quick Method election to reduce net remittance; (iv) ETA s. 156.1 'single filer' election for related corporations; and (v) treaty certification (Form NR301) to obtain reduced Canadian withholding tax on cross-border payments. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are governed by domestic anti-avoidance and the OECD Pillar Two Income Inclusion Rule once the CAD 750M-equivalent group revenue threshold is crossed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. E-15). Alberta does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and levies no provincial sales tax, so the operative indirect tax on Albertan MMORPG revenue is the 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the ETA s. 148(1) 'small supplier' threshold measured on total worldwide taxable supplies. Non-resident digital-economy suppliers (app-store game sales, subscriptions, virtual currencies) and platform operators must register once Canadian-source remote digital service supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar year (or on a rolling-quarter basis for newly commencing suppliers).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, XML digital stamping, or API-based government invoice pre-authorisation exists in Canada. GST/HST invoices may be paper or electronic; voluntary e-invoicing follows the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard (Peppol/OpenPeppol). Registrants must retain books and invoices for six years, file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or My Business Account, and remit through Canadian financial institutions. CRA relies on risk-based e-audits and data mining against app-store payout and customs data instead of invoice pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act to: (1) goods exported by the supplier (Part V); (2) intangible personal property, including digital game software, downloads, subscriptions and virtual items, supplied to a non-resident recipient for use wholly outside Canada (Part IX, places-of-supply rule in s. 142.1-142.2); and (3) services supplied to non-resident recipients for consumption outside Canada (other than services relating to Canadian real property or physically performed in Canada). An Alberta MMORPG publisher selling through Apple App Store and Google Play zero-rates supplies to non-resident end-users when platform territory and purchase data prove that the place of supply is outside Canada; supplies to Canadian resident players attract 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13/AAD) - required for physical exports and retained for mixed digital/physical collector editions; not generated for pure digital downloads
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill - evidence of shipment for physical media, servers or promotional hardware departing Canada

CRA zero-rating substantiation file - commercial invoices, Apple App Store / Google Play payout statements, territory purchase reports, and place-of-supply logs (IP address, storefront country, player residency) demonstrating use of the digital content outside Canada

Inward Remittance Certificate / FX remittance evidence - bank credit advices, SWIFT MT103 records and foreign-exchange conversion slips confirming receipt of foreign-currency proceeds and repatriation to the Alberta corporate bank account
GST/HST period return and reconciliation workpaper claiming the zero-rated export amount on the RT program account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess and claw back refunds within four years of the normal assessment date, extended to seven years for misrepresentation and unlimited for fraud. False zero-rating claims trigger ETA s. 280(1) 25% penalty on the tax that would have been payable, or s. 285 50% gross-negligence penalty where wilful blindness or deliberate false statements are shown, plus daily compound interest under s. 280.1. For income tax, s. 163(2) of the Income Tax Act imposes a 50% penalty on the understated Part I tax and ETA s. 327 allows criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment. Exporters must maintain the documentation bundle for six years and comply with CRA audit information requests within the statutory response period to avoid default assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing routine exchange controls. Relevant ancillary authorities include the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada for anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist-financing compliance, the Canada Revenue Agency for tax reporting and transfer-pricing administration, the Canada Border Services Agency for customs matters, and provincial securities regulators for derivatives and investment-dealer regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general requirement to obtain prior approval for foreign-currency purchases, dividend remittances, intercompany loans, royalty payments, service fees, capital contributions, loan repayments, or acquisition proceeds. Canadian-resident corporations may maintain foreign-currency accounts and remit funds offshore, subject to contractual bank controls, sanctions screening, beneficial-ownership verification, anti-money-laundering requirements, tax withholding, transfer-pricing rules, corporate-law solvency requirements, and financial-reporting obligations. Dividends, interest, royalties, and certain management or technical service fees paid to non-residents may require Canadian withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable income-tax treaty. The Canada-United States treaty and other treaties may reduce withholding rates, subject to beneficial-ownership, limitation-on-benefits, residence, and anti-avoidance conditions. Related-party financing and service arrangements must be supported by arm's-length terms and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. Payments connected with restricted jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, unusual virtual-asset flows, or opaque payment intermediaries may be delayed or rejected.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed deadline for converting export receipts into Canadian dollars. Export proceeds may generally remain in Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency accounts in Canada or abroad. The corporation must retain commercially reliable records supporting the underlying sale, customer, invoice, delivery, receipt, and tax treatment. Foreign-currency receipts must be translated for Canadian tax and financial-reporting purposes using an appropriate and consistently applied methodology. Cross-border payments must be screened for sanctions, anti-money-laundering concerns, applicable non-resident withholding tax, GST/HST treatment, transfer-pricing implications, and reporting requirements. Large international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, including related transactions aggregated within the applicable reporting period, may trigger reporting by the reporting entity to FINTRAC; this is not an export-conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary collection and payout functions; Low as the sole treasury bank. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment service provider may be used where its terms, licensing perimeter, correspondent arrangements, sanctions controls, and Canadian legal analysis permit the activity. It does not replace a Canadian operating bank for payroll, tax remittances, local supplier payments, statutory disbursements, or resilient treasury operations. A provider carrying on in-scope payment functions in Canada may be subject to registration and compliance obligations under the Retail Payment Activities Act administered by the Bank of Canada, in addition to applicable provincial, AML, sanctions, consumer-protection, privacy, and tax requirements. Apple App Store and Google Play proceeds should be paid to an account held in the legal name of the Alberta corporation, with platform contracts, payout reports, settlement statements, and reconciliation records retained. Offshore accounts and foreign assets may create Canadian tax, accounting, specified-foreign-property, transfer-pricing, and reporting considerations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal Canadian statutory requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available for an Alberta corporation, but the bank determines the process based on risk, ownership, residency, business model, document quality, and proposed transaction corridors. A bank may require an in-person meeting, notarized or certified documents, video verification, Canadian-resident signing authority, local address evidence, or enhanced due diligence. Directors, officers, signing authorities, beneficial owners, and controlling persons may be identified and verified under Canadian anti-money-laundering requirements. The corporation should maintain an Alberta registered office, a clear operating rationale, documented management authority, and a consistent explanation of its global MMORPG publishing and in-app-purchase settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, non-resident directors, or an ownership chain involving multiple holding companies or trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate or articles of incorporation, Alberta corporate registry profile, current corporate search, registers of directors and shareholders where maintained, organizational chart to the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners, passports and proof of address for relevant individuals, trust deeds or partnership agreements where applicable, beneficial-ownership declaration, board authorization, and written explanation of the commercial purpose of each entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loans, or repeated incoming transfers from founders, affiliates, or offshore accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreements, board resolutions, bank statements, audited or management financial statements, source-of-wealth evidence for material investors, tax residency information, financing documentation, transfer records, and a funds-flow diagram distinguishing equity, debt, revenue, refunds, and third-party collections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital entertainment and in-app-purchase revenue perceived as high-volume, intangible, or difficult to verify
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Game and publisher description, website and platform listings, Apple and Google agreements, payout statements, app-store transaction reports, customer terms, refund and chargeback policies, privacy policy, revenue-recognition memorandum, merchant-of-record analysis, expected monthly volumes, expected countries, chargeback controls, and bank-account reconciliation procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving numerous countries, payment aggregators, virtual-asset platforms, privacy-enhancing services, or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country and corridor matrix, counterparty list, sanctions-screening policy, prohibited-country list, transaction-monitoring rules, third-party payment-provider licenses, contractual chain, invoices, settlement reports, explanation of any intermediary, escalation procedure, and evidence that the corporation does not receive cryptocurrency unless expressly approved and appropriately controlled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among registered address, operating address, management location, IP footprint, and bank-account jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or office-service agreement, Alberta registered-office evidence, utility or service invoices, management and development-location schedule, employment or contractor agreements, payroll records where applicable, board minutes, corporate website, and an explanation of remote development, outsourced production, and global distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected turnover or transaction volume materially exceeds the financial statements or initial business plan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury forecast, twelve-month cash-flow model, platform payout forecasts, signed commercial contracts, pricing and user-acquisition assumptions, monthly reconciliation controls, tax-payment forecast, liquidity buffer policy, and periodic management reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for third-party payments, rapid pass-through transfers, cash withdrawals, or payments unrelated to the stated MMORPG publishing business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved payment matrix, delegated-authority policy, vendor master file, invoices and purchase orders, related-party register, exception-approval records, segregation-of-duties design, and written confirmation that the account will not be used as a payment intermediary or personal account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, chargeback, or law-enforcement concerns involving an owner, director, employee, customer, supplier, or payment provider
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity documents, screening results, beneficial-ownership analysis, risk assessment, compliance approvals, adverse-media response, contractual termination or mitigation evidence, sanctions legal review where appropriate, and documented escalation to the bank before initiating the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax-residency, FATCA, CRS, or Canadian tax-registration information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business number, GST/HST registration where applicable, corporate tax-residency statement, FATCA and CRS self-certifications, U.S. tax forms where applicable, treaty-residency evidence, non-resident withholding analysis, transfer-pricing policy, and authorization for the bank to update tax classifications.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian commercial bank account held in the exact legal name of the Alberta corporation. Use a documented capital-contribution or shareholder-loan agreement, board approval, accurate remitter and beneficiary information, and a payment narrative identifying the transaction as equity subscription, paid-in capital, or shareholder loan, as applicable. Canada does not prescribe a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate capital injections; the bank may nevertheless request an internal purpose code or transaction description. Provide the corporate registry extract, subscription or loan agreement, ownership chart, beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds evidence, and remittance instructions before transfer. Reconcile the incoming wire to the corporate ledger and issue appropriate share or debt documentation. Do not route capital through an employee, director, unrelated third party, personal wallet, or unapproved offshore EMI. The bank may report large international electronic funds transfers to FINTRAC and may apply sanctions, AML, tax, and correspondent-bank screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian domestic payment rails for Canadian suppliers and bank wires for international suppliers. For a normal service or software supplier, use a SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor message, with complete originator, beneficiary, invoice, purpose, intermediary-bank, and sanctions-screening information. For material software, platform, licensing, or development purchases with delivery or counterparty risk, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or controlled escrow arrangement as commercially appropriate. The bank may require purchase orders, invoices, contracts, shipping or delivery evidence where applicable, tax treatment, beneficial-owner information, and supporting documents for related-party payments. Confirm whether Canadian withholding tax applies to interest, royalties, or certain services paid to non-residents; obtain treaty documentation before applying a reduced rate. Maintain three-way matching among contract, invoice, and payment, and reconcile foreign-currency amounts and fees. Apple App Store and Google Play settlements should be reconciled against platform statements, refunds, commissions, withholding, chargebacks, and the net bank receipt.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, used for identifiable forecast receipts, payouts, expenses, or intercompany obligations and documented under suitable treasury or ISDA-style terms.

Non-deliverable forwards where the reference currency, settlement currency, counterparty, and applicable Canadian derivatives rules permit the transaction; the corporation should confirm eligibility, reporting, collateral, and trade-repository obligations with the dealer.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for documented financing or liquidity exposures, subject to counterparty eligibility, derivatives documentation, valuation, collateral, reporting, and accounting requirements.

Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for material and documented exposures where the corporation understands premium, exercise, liquidity, and accounting risks and the dealer confirms legal and suitability requirements.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion, supplier payments, tax payments, and platform proceeds; maintain an approved-counterparty list, transaction limits, hedge-designation policy, exposure forecast, confirmation controls, and independent valuation or reconciliation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Declaration of Registered Office and Directors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / Alberta Registries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or extra-provincial registration in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The corporation is marked in default; the Registrar may strike off or administratively dissolve the corporation after notice, typically for repeated failure to file annual returns. Certificates of compliance and status cannot be issued until the default is cured.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporate Income Tax Return (includes Alberta corporate tax administered by the CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end for a non-CCPC and 3 months after year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, repeat-filing penalty of 10%, interest on arrears, CRA collection enforcement, and potential director liability for unremitted withholdings. This does not trigger corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Alberta does not impose a revenue or asset threshold for audit. A mandatory independent audit is required only if the corporation is a distributing corporation offering securities to the public, if shareholders do not unanimously waive the auditor, if a shareholder requisition requires an audit, or if a court, regulator, lender, or payment network imposes the audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE for private non-distributing corporations. For the MMORPG scope, IFRS 15 / ASPE 3400 governs in-app purchase revenue and IAS 38 / ASPE 3064 governs game development costs; CRA requires tax-basis reconciliation on the T2 return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta Annual Return is the annual statutory confirmation of registered office and current directors. Share transfers must be entered in the Register of Members at transfer time, and significant-control changes must be recorded. Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO filing, but information on individuals with 25% or more voting control or other significant control must be kept current and produced to the Registrar or law enforcement on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–750 per year for a registered office and corporate agent service in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–12,000 per year if an independent audit is not waived; USD 0 if the non-distributing corporation validly dispenses with an auditor

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction for eligible CCPCs: Federal 9% and Alberta 2% on first CA$500,000 active business income (combined 11%); SR&ED refundable investment tax credit at 35% of qualified expenditures for CCPCs; no statutory tax holiday applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (combined federal-Alberta return) filed via CRA Corporation Internet Filing (CIF), Represent a Client, or certified service provider portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; payment instalments may be monthly or quarterly for large corporations, with final balance due at year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the GA/RC account number, taxable period, legal name and current registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must enter the assigned 15-character program account and the Canadian head office or authorized representative's address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate incorporation jurisdiction, corporate type, and country of central management and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark non-resident corporation and, if applicable, confirm the permanent establishment in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from all Canadian business and property sources, including in-app purchase receipts after platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment or on which Canadian-source income arises; attach T2S(91) allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deducting losses, reserves, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate jurisdiction net income to non-resident and Alberta portions; apply DTA treaty provisions for business profits under Article VII.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute federal and Alberta income tax payable using the applicable tax rate schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty withholding rate reductions and confirm Alberta provincial allocation factors when the permanent establishment is in Alberta.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of balance owing plus 1% for each full month late to a maximum of 12 months (s.162(2)); repeat late filers may face a 10% penalty; daily compound arrears interest under s.163.1 and failure-to-remit penalties up to 10%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, subject to tax treaty reductions (e.g., 5% under the Canada-US DTA for a 10%+ corporate shareholder; 15% for portfolio shareholders).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must submit Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty) and a current Certificate of Residence to the paying Canadian corporation before remittance. The payer may rely on the declaration, withholds at the lower treaty rate, reports the amount on Form NR4, and retains supporting documentation. The CRA may require confirmation from the treaty residence state's competent authority or additional Form NR302 information for specific benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for royalties (including software/IP licensing) and interest. Arm's-length interest payments enjoy a domestic exemption; treaty rates vary, generally 0% for certain copyright royalties and 10% for industrial royalties under the Canada-US DTA, while interest is frequently 0% for arm's-length lenders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No de minimis dollar threshold: Income Tax Act s.247(4) requires contemporaneous documentation for all controlled non-arm's-length cross-border transactions. Country-by-country reporting and Master File apply to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 1,000,000,000; documents must be produced within 3 months of CRA request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations; economic substance is tested through GAAR, sham doctrine, business purpose/factor tests, treaty-shopping limitations, and anti-hybrid/input-tax rules. An Alberta corporation must demonstrate actual Canadian substance before claiming DTA benefits for Canadian-sourced gaming revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Apple/Google App Store royalties or in-app purchase revenue from the T2; suppressing foreign bank accounts; using nominee directors to conceal business control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictment: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years (Income Tax Act s.239). Gross negligence: penalty equal to 50% of the understated tax (s.163.2); interest compounded daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns can be convicted as parties to the offense, personally fined or imprisoned; civil restitution via alter-ego claim allows corporate veil piercing if the corporation is an artificial instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring an offshore licensing company as a shell owner of MMORPG IP and setting excessive royalty or management charges to shift profit to a zero/low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment plus 10% penalty under s.247(3) where the aggregate adjustment exceeds the lesser of CA$50,000 or 10% of gross revenue; interest on reassessed tax; loss of treaty relief if beneficial ownership is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors authoring the offending transfer-pricing documentation may be personally assessed for failure to remit payroll or Part XIII deductions; knowingly understating income is an offence supporting personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Alberta 'corporate wrapper' with no office, employees, contracts, or substantive decision-making, solely to receive DTA benefits and avoid foreign withholding tax on MMORPG distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denies the tax benefit and allows reassessment; foreign tax denial under treaty abuse; administrative penalties for false statements; corporate dissolution or loss of name availability in jurisdictional filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the corporate form is characterized as a sham or alter ego, courts may pierce the veil and hold directors personally liable for unpaid taxes, torts, and foreign entity liabilities; restrictive travel may be imposed by foreign competent authorities in extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register or report under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act when operating a virtual currency exchange or money transfer service in connection with in-app payout rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 per case, criminal fine up to CAD 500,000 and 5 years imprisonment for officers and employees; mandatory enterprise and jurisdictional risk assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers can be charged when failure results from consent, neglect, or wilful blindness; directors may be personally barred from reincorporating or managing a financial business under FINTRAC licensing regimes.
